title: Sequences and eager collection operations
context: How do sequences differ from list operations like map and filter?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: List operations such as map and filter are eager: each step builds a full new list. Sequences process one element at a time through the whole chain, so intermediate lists are never built. Sequence operations are lazy and run only when a terminal operation such as toList, first or sum is called. Sequences help with large data or with a short-circuit like first. For small collections, lists are simpler and often just as fast.

points.title: Eager lists
points.why: Each list step creates a new full collection.

points.title: Lazy sequences
points.why: Elements flow through the chain one at a time, and nothing runs until a terminal operation.
